issues.legal_issue: A revision before the National Commission is not maintainable against a State Commission order in an appeal arising from execution proceedings after the consumer dispute has been finally adjudicated.
material_facts: The consumer dispute was finally adjudicated by the Supreme Court, which directed payment of interest, a refund, compensation, and litigation costs.
The complainant later initiated execution proceedings to enforce that final order.
The District Forum made a calculation in execution, and the State Commission altered that calculation in an appeal arising from the execution proceedings.
The Board filed a revision before the National Commission challenging the State Commission’s order.
issues.conclusion: The National Commission had no jurisdiction under Section 21(b) of the Consumer Protection Act, 1986 to entertain the revision. Execution proceedings are separate and independent enforcement proceedings, not a continuation of the consumer dispute.
issues.legal_principle: Section 21(b) of the Consumer Protection Act, 1986 confers revisional jurisdiction over orders in a consumer dispute pending before or decided by a State Commission; it does not provide for revision of an order in execution proceedings after the dispute has been finally adjudicated. Section 25(3) concerns enforcement of orders. A revision is a statutory remedy with narrower scope than an appeal, and execution proceedings are separate from the original suit or dispute. The Court relied on P.S. Sathappan (Dead) by LRs v. Andhra Bank Ltd. (2004) 11 SCC 672 on the statutory nature of the right to revision; Galada Power and Telecommunication Ltd. v. United India Insurance Co. Ltd. (2016) 14 SCC 161; Dattonpant Gopalvarao Devakate v. Vithalrao Maruthirao Janagaval (1975) 2 SCC 246 and Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Ltd. v. Dilbahar Singh (2014) 9 SCC 78 on the nature and scope of revisional jurisdiction; and affirmed the views in Guntupalli Rama Subbayya v. Guntupalli Rajamma, AIR 1988 AP 226, and Masomat Narmada Devi v. Nandan Singh, AIR 1987 Pat 33, that execution proceedings are not a continuation of the suit.

predicates.revision_challenges_execution_appeal_ord: A party seeks revision of a State Commission order made in an appeal arising from execution proceedings.
predicates.consumer_dispute_finally_adjudicated: The consumer dispute was finally decided before the challenged execution proceedings took place.
predicates.execution_started_to_enforce_final_order: A decree holder initiated proceedings to enforce the final order rather than to adjudicate the underlying consumer dispute.

issues.definition: When a party seeks revision of a State Commission order in an appeal from proceedings initiated to enforce a consumer dispute that has already been finally decided, the revision is not maintainable before the National Commission.
